rationale: With level 3+ already settled near 45% (with SI) and 38% (without), and level 2 counting anyone who lastingly loses one essential, roughly 1 in 100 people hit by a single chain over 75 years is more likely than not; the 20th century had three or four such events (1918 flu, WWII, the Great Leap famine, arguably HIV), though none since 1961. The extra level-2-only futures go mostly to slow-onset causes (climate, state breakdown, resources) and, without SI, to pandemics, while AI takeover stays largely bimodal so it gains little beyond its level-3 floor. The timeline assumes a roughly flat hazard of about 2% a year: AI and war risk peak mid-century, and climate harms build toward 2100.
